trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.location: Generalitat de Catalunya, 6, Sant Just Desvern, ES (41.3772,2.0791)

experiences.name: Sagrada Família Guided Tour
experiences.description: Explore Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica with a skip-the-line guided tour. Marvel at the intricate facades, stunning stained glass windows, and learn about the century-long construction history. Climb the towers for panoramic city views.

experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Barcelona's legendary public market on La Rambla. Sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, local cheeses, seafood, and fresh-squeezed juices from the vibrant stalls. A true feast for the senses and a cultural institution since 1217.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the L9 Sud metro line to Torrassa, then transfer to reach Sant Just Desvern area (budget option ~€5.50 vs €35+ taxi). Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the local neighbourhood to get oriented.

meals.lunch: N/A – in transit or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a budget-friendly dinner near the hotel – look for a local 'menú del día' (even available some evenings on Sundays) or a neighbourhood tapas bar. Budget ~€10–14. Try Bar Restaurant La Bodegueta de Sant Just if open, or a nearby supermarket (Mercadona/Lidl) for a quick self-catered meal under €6.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – you've just landed. Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€12.15) at the airport to save on all transport throughout the trip. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance as arrival is after 19:00.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour – Head into central Barcelona via metro (use your T-Casual card). Spend the morning on a self-guided or free walking tour of the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic). Explore the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30), Roman ruins of Barcino, Plaça Reial, and narrow medieval lanes. Arrive early (~9:00) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience – Walk up La Rambla to Mercat de la Boqueria. Browse the stalls, sample affordable fresh fruit, jamón, and local cheeses. Avoid the overpriced sit-down stalls – instead buy ingredients for a picnic (€5–8). Head to nearby Plaça de la Catalunya or Parc de la Ciutadella to enjoy your picnic lunch in the shade.
day_by_day.evening: Explore El Born neighbourhood on foot – visit the free exterior of Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar, browse indie boutiques, and soak up the atmosphere. As night falls, enjoy Barcelona's early nightlife scene: grab €3–4 craft beers at a bar in El Born (Bar del Pla or El Xampanyet are local favourites). Streets come alive after 22:00.

meals.breakfast: Café con leche and a croissant or tostada at a local café near the hotel or near the Gothic Quarter – budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Self-assembled picnic from La Boqueria market – fresh fruit, bread, cheese, and cured meats – budget €6–9.
meals.dinner: Menú del día at a local restaurant in El Born or Gothic Quarter – typically €12–15 for 3 courses with drink. Try Cervecería Catalana area or a side-street spot away from La Rambla.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks in the afternoon (up to 28.9°C) – carry water and wear sunscreen. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes. Free walking tours operate daily (tip-based, ~€5–10 tip suggested).

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Book skip-the-line tickets in advance online (€26–33 with tower access and audio guide; basic entry ~€26). Arrive at opening time (9:00) to avoid peak crowds and heat. The guided tour covers Gaudí's architectural genius, the Nativity and Passion facades, and the breathtaking interior forest of columns and stained glass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Eixample district on foot after the Sagrada Família. Walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the 'Block of Discord' – Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller exteriors are free to view. Peek at Casa Lleó Morera. If budget allows, the rooftop of Casa Batlló is stunning (€35+), but admiring from outside is free. Cool off in a local café with a €2–3 horchata or granizado.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Barceloneta beach for a sunset walk along the boardwalk (free). Watch the sun dip behind the city skyline. Grab a cheap beer from a beach kiosk (~€3). Later, explore the nightlife in the El Raval or Barceloneta area – bars open up fully after 22:00. Try Chiringuito del Mar or a beach bar for affordable drinks.

meals.breakfast: Toasted bread with tomato (pa amb tomàquet) and coffee at a café near the Sagrada Família – budget €4–6.
meals.lunch: Bocadillo (filled baguette) or falafel wrap from a takeaway near Eixample – budget €4–7. Eat in a shaded plaza.
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood paella or fideuà at a budget restaurant in Barceloneta – look for set menus around €13–16. Avoid the beachfront tourist traps; try side streets one block back.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família tickets online at least a week ahead – they sell out fast, especially in August. The interior is air-conditioned, a welcome relief from the heat. Wear light clothing and bring a refillable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell – Take the metro to Lesseps or Vallcarca and walk up to Park Güell (arrive by 8:00 for the free access zone, or budget €10 for the Monumental Zone ticketed area – book online). Enjoy Gaudí's mosaic terraces, the iconic dragon staircase, and panoramic views over Barcelona. The park is cooler and less crowded in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gràcia Neighbourhood Exploration – Walk downhill from Park Güell into the charming Gràcia barrio. Browse the Mercat de l'Abaceria (free to enter), explore bohemian plazas like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, and pop into independent shops and galleries. Rest in the shade during peak heat hours (14:00–16:00). Note: if visiting during the Festa Major de Gràcia (mid-August), the streets will be spectacularly decorated – a completely free cultural experience!
day_by_day.evening: Barcelona nightlife deep dive – Start with pre-drinks ('botellón' style or at a cheap bar) in Gràcia or El Raval around 21:00. Head to Sala Apolo, Razzmatazz, or City Hall club after midnight (entry €10–15, often includes one drink). Alternatively, enjoy free open-air live music events or street performances along La Rambla and El Born.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a pastry and coffee from a local bakery (forn de pa) in Gràcia – budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: Menú del día in Gràcia neighbourhood – excellent value at €11–14 for a full 3-course meal with wine. Try any local restaurant away from tourist areas.
meals.dinner: Light and cheap pre-night-out dinner: pintxos or tapas at a bar in El Raval – budget €8–12. Try Bar Marsella area or Carrer del Parlament for affordable options.

day_by_day.notes: Check if the Festa Major de Gràcia falls during your visit (usually 15–21 August) – if so, this is one of Barcelona's best free cultural events with elaborately decorated streets and free concerts. Nights are warm (~22–24°C), perfect for outdoor nightlife.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Hill – Take the metro to Paral·lel and ride the free Montjuïc funicular (included with metro T-Casual card). Visit the free Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic (€3.50 entry). Walk up to the Castell de Montjuïc for panoramic views over the city and port (€5 entry or free on first Sunday of the month). Enjoy the sea breeze and cooler temperatures at elevation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Poble Sec neighbourhood – Descend from Montjuïc into Poble Sec, one of Barcelona's most authentic and affordable barrios. Explore Carrer de Blai, famous for its pintxos bars where snacks start at €1–1.50 each. This is perfect for a cheap, delicious late lunch. Browse street art and the neighbourhood's laid-back vibe. Visit the free exterior of Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (a modernist architecture gem) if interested.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Barcelona – Return to the Gothic Quarter or El Born for a farewell stroll. Visit the free Magic Fountain of Montjuïc show if it runs that evening (Thursday shows in summer, check schedule – completely free). End the night with a final round of tapas and cañas (small beers) at a favourite spot discovered during the trip. Pack bags for departure.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and croissant or magdalenas at a café near the hotel – budget €3–5. Alternatively, buy pastries from a supermarket the night before for a €2 breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pintxos crawl on Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec – budget €8–12 for a filling selection of pintxos and a drink.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range local restaurant – splurge slightly on a menú de degustació or à la carte tapas. Budget €15–20. Try Cervecería Catalana, La Cova Fumada (cash only, arrive early), or any well-reviewed spot on TheFork app for discounts.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Magic Fountain schedule at barcelonaturisme.com – summer shows run Thursday to Sunday evenings and are completely free. If departing the next morning, prepare bags tonight. Keep remaining T-Casual metro trips for airport transfer. Total estimated daily spend (excluding Sagrada Família pre-booked ticket): €40–60/day including transport, food, and activities.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or L9 Sud metro to central Barcelona, then connect to Sant Just Desvern. Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll around the local neighbourhood to get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the hotel – try Bar Restaurant Can Ramonet or a local tapas bar in Sant Just Desvern for patatas bravas, pan con tomate, and a glass of house wine. Budget ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pick up a T-Casual metro card (10-trip card) at the airport or a nearby metro station to save money on public transport throughout the trip. Confirm all experience bookings for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Take the metro (L3 or L5) into central Barcelona and arrive early at Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. A skip-the-line guided tour (pre-booked) lets you explore the breathtaking nave, stained-glass windows, and Nativity and Passion facades without the crowds. Allow 2–2.5 hours. Tip: book tower access in advance for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration – Head uphill to Park Güell (book timed entry in advance). Wander the mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and Hypostyle Room, then descend into the charming Gràcia neighbourhood. Explore its bohemian plazas, independent boutiques, and colourful balconies at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach & El Born Nightlife Circuit – Catch the golden-hour sunset at Barceloneta Beach with a cold Estrella Damm from a beach chiringuito. As the city cools down (~21:00), make your way into the El Born district. Explore its lantern-lit medieval streets, pop into craft cocktail bars like Bar del Pla or Paradiso (ranked among the world's best bars), and soak up Barcelona's legendary nightlife energy.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia area or a local café near the Sagrada Família – coffee and a croissant or pa amb tomàquet. ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca – excellent tapas and montaditos in a buzzy setting. ~€18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born – a beloved cava bar serving anchovies, cheese, and tapas. Follow with pintxos hopping along Carrer del Parlament. ~€25–35 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks in the afternoon (up to 29°C) – carry a reusable water bottle and wear sunscreen. Park Güell's ticketed monumental zone sells out fast; book at least 2 weeks ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gràcia hills.

day_by_day.morning: La Boqueria Market Food Experience – Head to La Rambla early (by 09:30) before the tourist crowds peak. Immerse yourself in Barcelona's legendary covered market: sample fresh jamón ibérico, Manchego cheese, seasonal fruit, and local olives from the stalls. Grab a freshly made tapa or a glass of cava at one of the market bars. Allow 1.5–2 hours to browse and taste.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour – From La Boqueria, walk directly into the Gothic Quarter for a guided walking tour. Discover Roman ruins beneath the medieval streets, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, the old Jewish Quarter (El Call), and hidden courtyards. The tour typically lasts 2–2.5 hours and brings centuries of history to life. Afterwards, linger in Plaça de Sant Jaume and browse independent shops.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop aperitivo and Eixample architecture night walk – Enjoy a pre-dinner drink at a rooftop bar such as La Isabela (Hotel 1898) overlooking La Rambla, then stroll through the Eixample district as the sun sets to admire the Modernista architecture illuminated at night – Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) are dramatically lit after dark. End the evening at a relaxed restaurant in Eixample.

meals.breakfast: Inside La Boqueria Market – fresh fruit, a tostada with tomato and olive oil, and a cortado. ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Bar Cañete near the Parallel – traditional Catalan cuisine, excellent croquetas and fideuà. ~€20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza or Cervecería Catalana in Eixample – quality mid-range dining. Alternatively, Bodega Sepúlveda for Catalan wine and charcuterie boards. ~€22–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is best visited early; by 11:00 it becomes very crowded and some stalls cater more to tourists. The Gothic Quarter tour is most atmospheric in the morning light. Casa Batlló and La Pedrera offer ticketed evening 'magic nights' experiences – worth booking if architecture is a top priority.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Hill & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe – Take the Funicular de Montjuïc from Paral·lel metro station. Explore the hilltop: visit the Barcelona Pavilion (a masterpiece of modernist architecture by Mies van der Rohe), the Fundació Joan Miró for contemporary art, and the Montjuïc Castle for sweeping panoramic views over the city and port. The elevated position and morning breeze make this the coolest and most comfortable time to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Poblenou & @22 Innovation District Architecture Walk – Descend from Montjuïc and head to Poblenou, Barcelona's former industrial district now reinvented as a hub of cutting-edge contemporary architecture. Walk along Rambla del Poblenou, spot striking buildings like the Torre Glòries (Jean Nouvel's luminous tower), and explore street art and converted factory spaces. Stop at a rooftop pool bar if your hotel card grants access, or relax at a café before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach sunset swim & Port Olímpic nightlife – Cool off with a late-afternoon swim at Barceloneta Beach (the water is warmest in August). Watch the sunset from the sand, then head to Port Olímpic for dinner and Barcelona's famous club scene. The beachfront clubs (Opium, Pacha, Shoko) don't get going until midnight, so enjoy a leisurely dinner first and pace yourself.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café in Sant Just Desvern before heading out – coffee, orange juice, and a pastry. ~€6–10.
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, arrives early – it closes when food runs out) – legendary birthplace of the bombas (meat croquettes). ~€15–20 per person. Alternatively, a seafood restaurant on Passeig Marítim.
meals.dinner: La Mar Salada near Barceloneta – excellent paella and fresh seafood at mid-range prices. ~€28–38 per person. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: August is peak beach season – arrive at Barceloneta by 18:30 for a spot with a view. Port Olímpic clubs charge €15–25 entry and often include one drink. Carry cash as some smaller bars don't accept cards. Stay hydrated throughout the day – temperatures can feel higher near the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana & Sant Pere Neighbourhood – Start your final morning with a guided tour of the Palau de la Música Catalana, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the crown jewel of Catalan Art Nouveau architecture. The stained-glass skylight and ornate concert hall interior are jaw-dropping. Afterwards, explore the quiet Sant Pere neighbourhood nearby – less touristy than the Gothic Quarter, with lovely modernista buildings and local bakeries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure, souvenir shopping & farewell Vermouth – Spend the afternoon at your own pace. Browse the El Born boutiques for design souvenirs, visit the Mercat de Santa Caterina (a colourful alternative to La Boqueria), or return to any neighbourhood that captured your heart. At 13:00–15:00, join the beloved Barcelona tradition of the vermut: a pre-lunch vermouth with olives and chips at a traditional bar like Bar Calders or El Xampanyet.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample or El Born – Celebrate the end of a wonderful trip with a special dinner. Splurge slightly at a quality Catalan restaurant such as Bodega 1900 (Albert Adrià's vermouth bar-restaurant) or Disfrutar if budget allows. Enjoy the warm August evening at an outdoor terrace. Return to the hotel and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume or any neighbourhood bakery near the Palau – fresh croissant, café amb llet, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. ~€6–9.
meals.lunch: Vermut and pintxos at Bar Calders in Sant Antoni, or a set lunch menu (menú del día) at a local restaurant – typically €13–16 for three courses with wine.
meals.dinner: Bodega 1900 in Eixample – creative Catalan tapas in an elegant setting. ~€35–50 per person. Book in advance. For a more relaxed option, try Bormuth in El Born for tapas and natural wines at ~€25–30.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure details and arrange transport back to the airport in advance – the Aerobus runs from Plaça Catalunya every 5–10 minutes and takes ~35 minutes. Leave at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight. Store luggage at the hotel until you're ready to leave. The Palau de la Música tour must be booked ahead; morning slots are most available.

meals.dinner: Late dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nearby upscale local spot such as El Celler de Can Roca's sister bistro concept in the area — alternatively, request the hotel concierge to recommend a premium Sant Just Desvern restaurant open late, such as a traditional Catalan gastrobar with charcuterie boards, pa amb tomàquet, and a bottle of Priorat red wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm all upcoming tour bookings with the concierge upon check-in. Request a private driver or premium taxi account for the week. Opt for tower access to enjoy panoramic views over Barcelona's Eixample grid. Spend approximately 2–2.5 hours exploring the Nativity and Passion facades, the luminous nave, and the crypt museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — After a leisurely lunch, head to Park Güell for a guided exploration of the mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and the Monumental Zone. End the night at a rooftop terrace bar such as the Rooftop at Hotel Arts for sweeping sea views.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the hotel or a café con leche and croissant at a local Eixample patisserie near Sagrada Família
meals.lunch: Alkimia or Lasarte (Michelin-starred, Eixample) — contemporary Catalan cuisine with a refined tasting menu; reserve in advance
meals.dinner: El Xiringuito Escribà on Barceloneta Beach for premium seafood and paella, followed by drinks in El Born

Discover Roman ruins beneath the Plaça del Rei, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, the ancient Jewish Quarter (El Call), and hidden courtyards. Sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, artisan cheeses, fresh-squeezed juices, and Catalan specialties with a knowledgeable local food guide. day_by_day.afternoon_extension: Visit Palau de la Música Catalana — a UNESCO World Heritage modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Take a premium guided tour of the stunning stained-glass interior.

For a sophisticated late night, visit Opium Barcelona or Pacha Barcelona for a VIP table experience.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia or Federal Café in the Gothic Quarter — artisan coffee and a full Catalan breakfast
meals.lunch: Bar Pinotxo inside La Boqueria — iconic market counter dining with fresh seafood and daily specials; or a premium pintxos spread curated during the food experience
meals.dinner: Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars) or Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas bar) — book months in advance; experience molecular gastronomy and creative Catalan cuisine

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is extremely crowded mid-morning in August — the food experience guide will help navigate and access the best stalls. Palau de la Música Catalana tours should be pre-booked. For VIP nightlife, contact the hotel concierge to arrange table reservations at clubs — dress code is smart-casual to formal.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc & Architectural Gems — Take the Montjuïc cable car or a private car up to the hill for panoramic views over the city and port. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert. Continue to the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe — the reconstructed Barcelona Pavilion, a masterpiece of modernist architecture and a must for architecture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Passeig de Gràcia Modernisme Walk — Descend to Barcelona's most elegant boulevard for a self-guided or private guided tour of the 'Block of Discord': Casa Batlló (book the premium 'Magic Nights' experience or the standard premium tour with AR glasses), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Continue to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) for a rooftop tour with views of Gaudí's iconic chimneys — particularly spectacular in the afternoon light. Explore the upscale boutiques on Passeig de Gràcia between tours.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop of La Pedrera (if attending the evening 'La Pedrera by Night' event) or at the rooftop bar of the Hotel Majestic on Passeig de Gràcia. Dinner in the upscale Eixample district, followed by a sophisticated evening at a jazz club such as Jamboree Jazz Club in the Gothic Quarter or a premium wine bar for a curated Catalan and Spanish wine tasting.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Brunch at Parking Pizza (Sant Antoni) — one of Barcelona's trendiest brunch spots with premium ingredients
meals.lunch: Bodega Sepúlveda or Cervecería Catalana (Eixample) — premium Catalan tapas, seafood, and vermouth in a stylish setting
meals.dinner: ABaC Restaurant & Hotel (Michelin-starred, Sarrià) — one of Barcelona's finest tasting menus with creative Mediterranean cuisine; private taxi required

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló's 'Magic Nights' rooftop experience (summer evenings) is one of Barcelona's most unique premium experiences — book well in advance. La Pedrera's 'El Cel de la Pedrera' evening concert series on the rooftop is also highly recommended in August. Comfortable but stylish footwear essential for the cobblestone and tile surfaces.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning and hotel checkout preparation. Enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. If time permits, take a final swim in the hotel pool or a morning walk in the peaceful Sant Just Desvern surroundings. Pack and prepare for departure or onward travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Barcelona experience — return to the city for a last afternoon. Visit the Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC) on Montjuïc for its world-renowned Romanesque art collection and the spectacular view of the city from the terrace. Alternatively, spend the afternoon shopping for premium Catalan products — artisan olive oil, wines, cured meats, and design objects — at upscale delis on Carrer d'Enric Granados or the Eixample.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Barcelona's most iconic fine-dining establishments. Toast to the trip with a bottle of Catalan cava or a Grand Reserva Rioja. If departing the following day, enjoy a final nightcap at a rooftop bar with city views — the Eclipse Bar at Hotel W Barcelona (the sail-shaped tower on the waterfront) offers one of the most dramatic sunset and evening panoramas in the city.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast — request a premium spread with fresh fruit, smoked salmon, Catalan cheeses, and cava if desired
meals.lunch: Informal but premium farewell lunch at Cervecería Catalana or a terrace restaurant on Passeig de Gràcia — enjoy patatas bravas, gambas al ajillo, and a final glass of Albariño
meals.dinner: Moments (Mandarin Oriental Barcelona, Michelin-starred) — refined Catalan haute cuisine in an elegant setting on Passeig de Gràcia; the perfect luxury send-off dinner

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if the afternoon is still free. Book a private transfer back to El Prat Airport well in advance — allow at least 60–90 minutes travel time from Sant Just Desvern during August peak traffic. The Eclipse Bar at Hotel W requires smart dress and can be busy on summer evenings — arrive before 21:00 for the best sunset views.
